title: "File format"
description: "How a studyflow is stored: the canonical YAML source, its lossless projection to BPMN 2.0 XML, and images that carry the study inside them."
---

![The files that carry a whole study, and what converts into what. Thick arrows are the lossless hops.](../assets/img/diagrams/file-format.svg){#fig-round-trip fig-alt="A flowchart. The modeler's diagram saves as .studyflow.yaml and lowers to .bpmn BPMN 2.0 XML, and those two convert into each other losslessly in both directions. The modeler also renders to .studyflow.png and .studyflow.svg, which carry two payloads beside the pixels: the same BPMN XML as embedded source, and a draw.io copy of the drawing. An image reopens in the modeler from its embedded source, never from its pixels. Dotted arrows leave the round trip: the draw.io payload downloads on its own as .drawio, and the modeler exports one way to LinkML, NIDM-Results, and ARTEM-IS."}

| File | Carries | Reopens as a studyflow |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `.studyflow.yaml` | the study itself, in full — **the canonical form** | yes |
| `.bpmn` | the same study, as standard BPMN 2.0 XML | yes |
| `.studyflow.png` | a raster picture, and the study inside it | yes |
| `.studyflow.svg` | a vector picture, and the study inside it | yes |
| `.drawio`, `.linkml.yaml`, `.nidm.ttl`, `.artemis.json` | a document derived for another tool | no |

The YAML is the source of truth and the XML its interoperability projection; the two convert losslessly in both directions. Keep the YAML in version control — everything else is derived from it.

## The canonical form

The study is written as YAML, following whichever element sets are loaded.

| Rule | In the file |
|:--|:--|
| containment becomes nesting | a study's steps are written inside the study |
| references are written as ids | `sourceRef: Enrolled`, not a second copy of the element |
| anything unrecognized is kept | a key no loaded set declares is preserved and reported, never dropped |
| defaults are omitted | a value equal to its declared default is left out, and restored on read |
| inferable types are omitted | `type:` appears only where the element is not the type already expected there |

| Top-level key | Holds |
|:--|:--|
| `id` | the identifier of the document |
| `definitions` | the document's remaining attributes, namespace declarations included |
| *any other key* | one root element — a process, a collaboration — keyed by its id |
| `elements` | root elements that cannot be keyed, because the id collides with a reserved key |
| `diagram` | geometry that could not be attached to the element it positions |

A file with no `definitions` key is not read as a studyflow. There is no separate version key: the format version is the version segment of the core namespace, which `definitions` carries.

```yaml
id: minimal_study
definitions:
  targetNamespace: http://bpmn.io/schema/bpmn

Minimal_Study:
  type: bpmn:Process
  name: Minimal study
  extensionElements:
    - type: studyflow:Study
  flowElements:

    Enrolled:
      type: bpmn:StartEvent
      name: Enrolled and consented
      consentFormUri: https://example.org/protocols/minimal-study/consent.md

    Flanker:
      type: bpmn:Task
      name: Flanker
      extensionElements:
        - type: cognitive:CognitiveTask
          instrument: jspsych
          implementation: https://github.com/jspsych/jspsych-contrib@v0.4.0#flanker

    Done:
      type: bpmn:EndEvent
      name: Done
      redirectTo: https://app.prolific.com/submissions/complete?cc={COMPLETION_CODE}
      completionCodeType: dynamic

    Flow_Enrolled_Flanker:
      type: bpmn:SequenceFlow
      sourceRef: Enrolled
      targetRef: Flanker
    Flow_Flanker_Done:
      type: bpmn:SequenceFlow
      sourceRef: Flanker
      targetRef: Done
```

That is [`minimal_study.studyflow.yaml`](../assets/examples/minimal_study.studyflow.yaml) in full. Geometry is optional: layout follows from `sourceRef` and `targetRef`, and a file arriving without coordinates is laid out on open.

## Six short forms

| What you write | What it stands for |
|:--|:--|
| a YAML mapping under `additionalArguments`, `values`, `configurations`, or a schema `body` | the same YAML, as one quoted string |
| a plain list under `extensionElements` | `bpmn:ExtensionElements` holding that list |
| `bounds`, `label`, and `waypoint` on the element itself | a separate geometry record elsewhere in the file |
| elements keyed by id under `flowElements` | a list of elements, each carrying its own `id` |
| a condition or expression written as a plain string | an expression element carrying nothing but that string |
| `documentation`, and `checklist` for the checklist entry | BPMN documentation entries, one marked as the checklist |

Each collapses only where nothing is lost, and the long form is still accepted. All six at once:

```yaml
flowElements:                    # elements addressed by id
  Split_Train_Test:
    type: bpmn:ServiceTask
    extensionElements:           # a plain list, nothing enclosing it
      - type: functional:Transform
        operationType: split
    checklist: |-                # the documentation entry marked as the checklist
      - [ ] Test split held out
    implementation: python://sklearn.model_selection.train_test_split
    additionalArguments:         # YAML written as YAML
      test_size: 0.25
      random_state: 42
    dataInputAssociations:
      DataInput_Stratify:
        sourceRef:
          - target
        transformation: stratify # an expression, as a plain string
    bounds:                      # geometry, on the thing it positions
      x: 582
      "y": 230
```

Converting a file to XML and back returns byte-identical text for every example shipped with the modeler, so a diff shows edits rather than churn:

```diff
         - type: cognitive:CognitiveTask
           instrument: jspsych
-          implementation: https://github.com/jspsych/jspsych-contrib@v0.4.0#flanker
+          implementation: https://github.com/jspsych/jspsych-contrib@v0.5.0#flanker
```

## The BPMN 2.0 XML projection

Studyflow's additions ride in two places the standard reserves: a research type sits inside `extensionElements`, and an added field is a namespaced attribute. A generic BPMN tool ignores whatever it does not recognize.

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<bpmn:definitions xmlns:bpmn="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL" xmlns:studyflow="http://behaverse.org/schemas/studyflow/v1" xmlns:cognitive="http://behaverse.org/schemas/studyflow/cognitive" id="minimal_study" targetNamespace="http://bpmn.io/schema/bpmn">
  <bpmn:process id="Minimal_Study" name="Minimal study">
    <bpmn:extensionElements>
      <studyflow:study />
    </bpmn:extensionElements>
    <bpmn:startEvent id="Enrolled" name="Enrolled and consented" studyflow:consentFormUri="https://example.org/protocols/minimal-study/consent.md">
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_Enrolled_Flanker</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:startEvent>
    <bpmn:task id="Flanker" name="Flanker">
      <bpmn:extensionElements>
        <cognitive:cognitiveTask instrument="jspsych" implementation="https://github.com/jspsych/jspsych-contrib@v0.4.0#flanker" />
      </bpmn:extensionElements>
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_Enrolled_Flanker</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_Flanker_Done</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:task>
    <bpmn:endEvent id="Done" name="Done" studyflow:redirectTo="https://app.prolific.com/submissions/complete?cc={COMPLETION_CODE}" studyflow:completionCodeType="dynamic">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_Flanker_Done</bpmn:incoming>
    </bpmn:endEvent>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Enrolled_Flanker" sourceRef="Enrolled" targetRef="Flanker" />
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_Flanker_Done" sourceRef="Flanker" targetRef="Done" />
  </bpmn:process>
</bpmn:definitions>
```

Data associations are written out in the standard's own long form and folded back on read.

## Images that carry the study

| Export | What travels beside the pixels |
|:--|:--|
| `.studyflow.png` | the study as standard BPMN 2.0 XML, and a draw.io copy of the drawing |
| `.studyflow.svg` | the same two, the draw.io copy in draw.io's own editable-SVG form |

The whole object travels — meaning and geometry alike. What does not travel is the element sets themselves, or any data the study produced. Turn the source payload off and the image is a picture and nothing more; an image that has been through a screenshot tool or a vector editor keeps the pixels and loses the study. The embedded source, never the rendering, is authoritative.

An export that carries the study also stamps who exported it and when. A derived document carries no stamp.

## Everything read and written

| Format | Extension | For | Read back |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Studyflow | `.studyflow.yaml` | the study itself | yes, also `.studyflow` |
| BPMN 2.0 XML | `.bpmn` | other BPMN 2.0 tooling | yes, also `.xml` |
| SVG | `.studyflow.svg` | a vector figure that reopens as the study | yes, also `.svg` |
| PNG | `.studyflow.png` | a raster figure that reopens as the study | yes, also `.png` |
| draw.io | `.drawio` | further editing as a general-purpose drawing | no |
| LinkML schema | `.linkml.yaml` | the study's data elements as a LinkML schema | no |
| NIDM-Results | `.nidm.ttl` | analysis metadata as RDF, for neuroimaging tooling | no |
| ARTEM-IS | `.artemis.json` | an EEG methods descriptor, for reporting | no |
| jsPsych timeline | `.json` | building a studyflow from an existing timeline | read only |
